transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-11
- Start: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~52m
- Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (Head of ML, Ridgetrail), Priya Desai (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Finance)

Summary notes (auto): Jordan opened with context, Maya demoed console, customer asked security and billing questions, ended with pilot ask and next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Evan: good morning, thanks. excited to see the console walkthrough.
[00:12] Priya: hey all, we've got 30 minutes of internal context then we'll jump into product.
[00:18] Jordan: perfect, we'll keep it practical. agenda — quick qualification, demo per-route dashboards, cost mapping, then Q&A and next steps.
[02:05] Maya: ok jumping in on the console — this is the routes view, think of "route" as a logical path in your app, e.g., chat-bot-2, embeddings-search, ingestion-transformer. you can tag routes and they flow through telemetry to the usage lens.
[03:00] Priya: quick question, we currently send requests to a central endpoint and tags are set in our app layer. will that mapping work?
[03:12] Maya: yes, the SDK supports per-request metadata headers, and we also accept route names in the body. if you prefer, we can map based on JWT claims or your internal request ID.
[04:10] Evan: what's the latency impact when we enable per-request metadata? our SLAs are tight.
[04:22] Maya: negligible — it's just additional metadata. the bigger latency levers are batching and model choice. we can keep you on the lower-latency routing tier. note: continuous batching is configurable per-route.
[05:30] Liam: from finance's perspective, we want to break spend down to product lines and owners. how granular is the console?
[05:45] Maya: you can slice by route, model, customer tag, region, and even by tokenizer steps. the cost model uses per-token cost plus infra attribution; we show attribution to GPU pool for Dedicated customers.
[06:40] Priya: can we import our cost center codes?
[06:48] Jordan: yes you can map route tags to cost center codes; we have a mapping spreadsheet template — I'll share the CSV.
[08:00] Maya: demoing the Route Spend Map — here's a Sankey-like visualization that shows traffic from routes to models and then to GPU pools. you can hover to see tokens, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[09:10] Evan: that Sankey's helpful. does the console estimate caching savings? we have a lot of repeated prefixes.
[09:22] Maya: yes we surface suggested cache hits and estimated savings if you enable prefix or KV cache. estimate is based on your historical prefix similarity and shows projected token savings.
[10:40] Priya: about hosted vs dedicated — our legal team wants isolation but cost predictability too. what's your recommendation?
[10:52] Jordan: common pattern is start hosted to iterate, then commit to Dedicated for heavy steady traffic. Dedicated gives you GPU pool attribution, predictable throughput, and optional VPC peering.
[11:20] Evan: what about private deployments? we have some data-regulated flows.
[11:30] Maya: we offer Private (VPC or on-prem) with a customer-controlled control plane. integrates with KMS for key management and we've done HSM integrations for a couple customers.
[12:05] Liam: security — can we get audit logs and retention options? SOC2?
[12:12] Jordan: yes we provide audit logs, configurable retention windows, SSO via SAML/Okta, and SOC 2 Type II evidence. we'll send the security whitepaper and the cert links after the call.
[13:45] Priya: great. for billing formats — can Redwood emit a route-level CSV we can ingest to our FinOps tooling?
[13:55] Maya: absolutely — there is an export button and an API. the CSV includes columns: timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, infra_attrib, cost_usd, cost_center (if mapped).
[15:03] Evan: do you do cost re-allocation for shared infra? we have shared batching across routes.
[15:12] Maya: yes we attribute infra costs by kernel usage and time-sliced GPU allocation, then prorate to routes by active tokens and KV cache hits. it's an approximation but we expose the calculation and you can reweight it.
[16:40] Jordan: demoing the per-route breakdown page now — top of page shows traffic trend, cost trend, unit cost, Wasted tokens (retries / transcripts), and recommended optimizations.
[18:05] Priya: what's your definition of wasted tokens?
[18:12] Maya: token retries, aborted requests, and long-running context truncations where the model consumed a lot of prompt but returned minimal unique output.
[19:30] Liam: what's the recommended optimization path for a high-per-token route?
[19:40] Maya: 1) enable caching / prefix cache, 2) try a smaller quantized model for non-critical outputs, 3) tune max tokens and stop sequences, 4) use routing policies to send low-criticality traffic to cheaper regions/models.
[21:02] Evan: can we run an A/B to measure quality delta between quantized model and full FP16?
[21:12] Maya: yes — the rollout tooling supports canaries and A/B; you can wire metrics to our evals or your own quality signals.
[22:30] Priya: about quotas — can we set per-route spend caps or throttles to avoid cost spikes?
[22:40] Jordan: yep per-route budgets, alerts, and throttles. you can set a hard cap or soft alerts with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants.
[24:05] Evan: are there examples of customers that saved materially by switching routing policies?
[24:15] Maya: yes, a retail customer reduced per-token spend by ~30% using caching + dedupe routing and moving bulk embeddings to a quantized model. I'll attach that case study link.
[25:00] Priya: show me the mapping workflow from our billing CSV to your route names.
[25:12] Maya: sure — we have a mapping UI where you upload your CSV, map your cost center column to route tags, and the console shows a diff preview before applying.
[27:30] Liam: from compliance, data residency — can we pin data to EU regions?
[27:40] Jordan: yes region pinning is supported; Private deployments give you full data locality control. Hosted supports region scoping with EU-only data planes.
[29:10] Evan: question about model kernels and sequence length — for long context runs we see token spikes and GPU cost. how do you pick kernels?
[29:22] Maya: our runtime selects kernels based on model shape, sequence length distribution and hardware. for large seqs we recommend memory-optimized pools and we show kernel selection in the telemetry for debugging. occasionally transcribe as "K V cache" in the UI but that's the KV cache.
[31:05] Priya: can we get sample per-route telemetry for 48 hours to run offline analysis?
[31:12] Jordan: yes — Maya will run a 48-hour route-slice simulator if you provide sample traffic. that's our normal pilot benchmark to show expected cost and latency.
[32:40] Evan: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated capacity?
[32:50] Jordan: depends on region and size but typically 2-6 weeks once contract is signed. we can provision initial burst capacity while Dedicated is being stood up.
[34:00] Priya: procurement question — do you support net-30 and PO?
[34:08] Jordan: yes enterprise billing supports PO and net terms; we'll include pricing options in the follow-up.
[35:20] Liam: can you show the route-level anomaly detection? we had a big spike last month that killed budgets.
[35:30] Maya: on the Alerts tab you can configure anomaly detection by baseline plus sensitivity. when a route spikes beyond the threshold the system can trigger a webhook, slack alert, or auto-throttle. we also keep a forensic view with raw requests to help triage.
[37:05] Evan: any gotchas with our existing kong/ingress and the SDK?
[37:15] Priya: we run Kong at the edge.
[37:20] Maya: common architecture works fine; we have examples for Kong and envoy. if you need a sidecar approach to inject tags we can demo that.
[39:00] Jordan: quick note on cost modeling — the console splits bill into token-level compute cost and infra overhead; infra overhead includes GPU amortization, storage for KV caches, and networking. you can toggle to show raw compute-only dollars.
[40:30] Evan: where do we see quantization recommendations?
[40:36] Maya: Optimize tab shows model and quantization recommendations per route, plus a predicted quality delta. you can run a calibration job to check latency and perplexity tradeoffs.
[41:45] Priya: show me a sample CSV export.
[41:52] Maya: downloads... here is the export that includes per-request lines and aggregated rows.
[42:15] Jordan: linking to the mapping guide and the sample CSV in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/console-route-mapping and https://redwood.ai/samples/route-billing-sample.csv
[43:05] Liam: ok, what are the blockers from our side to start a pilot?
[43:12] Evan: we need security docs, a trial agreement, and a billing sample.
[43:20] Jordan: we will send the security package and the pilot SOW. Maya will prepare the simulator run plan.
[44:00] Priya: timeline wise, if we get data by Monday can we start the 48hr run the following Thursday?
[44:10] Maya: yes that's feasible.
[45:30] Evan: a couple of quick objections — our infra team is worried about vendor lock-in and about the accuracy of cost attribution. how do we address that?
[45:40] Jordan: for lock-in we support open standards, you can export all telemetry and mappings. attribution is transparent, we show the math and let you re-weight. also Dedicated and Private deployments mitigate lock-in concerns for infra control.
[47:05] Priya: can we get a short legal-friendly summary of retention and deletion policies for customer data?
[47:14] Jordan: yes we'll include that in the security pack.
[48:00] Maya: final quick tips — start with a small set of top 5 routes, map them to cost centers, run the 48hr simulator, enable prefix caching on chat routes, and run an A/B on quantized models for embeddings.
[49:20] Evan: sounds good. Liam and I will align on what to share and we'll get Priya to upload the CSV.
[50:00] Jordan: recap of next steps: we'll send security whitepaper and SOC2 link, send pilot SOW and pricing, Maya will plan the simulator, Ridgetrail to provide anonymized billing CSV. we'll aim to kick the pilot week of 3/18.
[51:10] Liam: thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
[51:20] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite and assets. bye.
